subject: Post-call: latency & throughput discovery — measurement definitions and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@acmeretail.com>; Devon Park <devon.park@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: latency & throughput discovery — measurement definitions and next steps

Claire / Devon — thanks again for the sync earlier. Quick recap and proposed way forward so we can get a reproducible qualification run scheduled: 

Summary of what we heard (please flag anything I missed):
- Target SLO: p95 generation latency <= 120ms for standard user prompts (median prompt length ~180 tokens / 256 max).
- Sustained throughput requirement: 120 qps for the shopping-recommendations endpoint during peak windows.
- Concurrent sessions: expected steady concurrency of ~12 with short spikes to 40 during promotional events; warm-start behavior important for spike handling.
- Streaming requirement: incremental output enabled (chunked tokens). Tail-token latency target: p95 tail <= 40ms when streaming enabled.

Proposed measurement approach (high level):
1) Use a stable prompt set (attached) that represents 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long prompts — please confirm the distribution.
2) Run three phases: cold start ramp, steady-state sustained run (30m), and spike window (5m simulated bursts).
3) Capture per-request timing: request-accept, first-byte, last-byte, and server-side processing breakdown (queue, decode, KV fetch).
4) Report p50/p95/p99 for both generation latency and streaming tail, plus error rates and token cost metrics.

Attachments I’m sharing: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompts), measurement-spec-20261109.md (detailed metrics & definitions), eval-harness-config.yaml (starter harness config).

Next steps / ask: 
- Claire: confirm the prompt distribution above and whether we should add a shopping-cart personalization prompt (I can include if you want).
- Devon: confirm whether Procurement wants the qualification done on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated pool (impacts test account & billing).
- Marcus/Monica: please review the measurement spec and suggest any additional counters we should collect (especially around KV cache hit rates / prefix cache behavior).

I’ll schedule the benchmark kickoff once we hear back on the two clarifications. Thanks — looking forward to getting this reproducible so your SREs can validate.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Huang <claire@acmeretail.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Park <devon.park@acmeretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & throughput discovery — measurement definitions and next steps

Thanks Lauren — useful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt distribution looks right; please add a personalization prompt that includes cart context (user_id + last 3 items) — that will likely exercise KV cache paths.
- For concurrency: we need the spike window to include a 3x concurrency burst (we see 12 steady -> 36 for ~3 minutes during promos).
- Warm start: our infra will sometimes scale pods; can you include a cold-start scenario where the model’s KV cache is empty? We want to quantify cold vs warm behavior.

One more ask: our security team has a short questionnaire for Hosted vs Dedicated runs (data residency + audit logs). Devon will loop them in.

Appreciate the artifacts — we’ll review the prompt set and get back with a few edits by EOD tomorrow.

— Claire
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Devon Park <devon.park@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & throughput discovery — measurement definitions and next steps

Claire — perfect, thanks for the details. A couple of notes in response: 

- I’ve added a new prompt "cart_personalize_long" to acme_prompt_set_v1.json so that we exercise prefix/KV paths.
- measurement-spec-20261109.md now includes explicit definitions for: request-accept, first-byte, last-byte, server-queue, decode-time, kv-lookup, and stream-flush.
- For cold-starts we’ll run two variants: (A) cold KV (fresh process, no prefetched embeddings) and (B) warm KV (prefetched prefixes). We’ll tag traces accordingly so it’s easy to filter.
- Spike scenario: we’ll do a scripted 3x concurrency burst for 3 minutes followed by 10m of ramp-down.

Practical ask: please confirm which environment you want the canonical run in (hosted vs dedicated). If Hosted, we’ll provide a sandbox API key with usage tracking; Dedicated will require capacity reservation and a short procurement approval.

I’ve also pushed a starter harness config to the repo (link below) that maps your endpoints, auth, and the prompt set. If you’re okay I’ll propose two benchmark windows (Tue 11/17 09:00–11:00 PT for cold-starts + Wed 11/18 02:00–03:00 PT for spike simulation) — tentative until you confirm environment.

Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/acme-onboarding (starter harness)

— Lauren

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME qualification — tasks and owners

Team — quick internal note after Claire’s confirmation:

Action items:
- Marcus: prep the sandbox Hosted API keys and quota window; coordinate with Claire on rate limits. (owner)
- Monica: review measurement-spec-20261109.md and add KV cache counters + tail-latency tracing annotations; validate that our harness captures stream flush timestamps. (owner)
- Lauren: schedule the benchmark windows after Claire confirms environment; create a short runbook for the Acme SREs showing how to reproduce locally. (owner)

Constraints / risks to flag for Sales lead: procurement may prefer Dedicated which could push the canonical run by ~2 weeks. Also security questionnaire might require a short-delegation for log-review access.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal with the proposed dates and attach the artifacts.

— Lauren
